images.title: Three rotis, four children
images.purpose: Set up the question: 3 rotis, each cut into 4 equal pieces, waiting to be shared equally among 4 children.
images.composition: A row of three rotis across the top, a row of four empty plates below with wide white space, and one question line at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 3 round rotis of exactly the same size, evenly spaced, each cut by two straight lines into 4 equal pieces, all pieces plain with outlines teal #0072B2. Bottom row: 4 empty round plates of the same size, evenly spaced, outlined amber #E69F00. No pieces are moved onto the plates and nothing is shaded. Caption at the left of each row; question line centred at the bottom. No children drawn. Exactly 3 rotis, 12 equal pieces, 4 plates.
labels: how much roti for each child?

images.takeaway: Cut each roti into 4 equal pieces, then share all the pieces equally among 4 plates.
images.description: Three rotis each cut into 4 equal pieces above 4 empty plates, with the captions 3 rotis and 4 children and the question how much roti for each child?
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count all the pieces and say how many pieces each plate should get.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the rotis already cut into fourths beside 4 plates gives the child a sharing method without the answer.
